hook: The Duke of Normandy who won England at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

pages.x: William was born around 1028 at Falaise in Normandy, son of Duke Robert and Herleva, a tanner's daughter. Called "the Bastard", he became duke at about seven when his father died on pilgrimage. Three of his guardians were murdered, and he grew up tough.

His cousin, Edward the Confessor of England, had no children, and William said Edward had promised him the crown, and that the English earl Harold had sworn on holy relics to support him. But when Edward died in January 1066, Harold was crowned king.

In September 1066 William crossed the Channel with about 7,000 men and their horses. On 14 October near Hastings he met Harold, who had just beaten a Norwegian invasion in the north. When a rumour spread that William was dead, he lifted his helmet to show his face. By evening Harold was dead and the English broke.

William was crowned king of England on Christmas Day 1066 in Westminster Abbey. When the crowd inside shouted its approval, Norman guards outside thought it was a riot and set fire to the houses nearby.

The English rebelled, and in 1069 to 1070 William crushed the north of England, burning villages, crops and animals; perhaps 100,000 people starved. He built castles everywhere, among them the Tower of London, and gave English land to his Norman lords.

In 1086 he sent officials across England to record who owned every piece of land, and how many people, ploughs, pigs and mills were on it. It was so thorough that the English compared it to the Last Judgement, Domesday. It is still kept in the National Archives.

He died in 1087 after a fall from his horse in France. At his funeral in Caen, his swollen body would not fit into the stone coffin. When the monks pushed, it burst, and the smell drove everyone out of the church.

The Norman Conquest changed England for ever. Normans replaced the English nobles, castles rose across the land, and French words like beef, court and justice poured into English. Every English monarch since descends from him.
